name: Jamaica
prevalence_note: Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF ALSU / Fraud Squad) & Bank of Jamaica (BOJ) 2025-2026: advance-fee lottery/prize clearance calls, commercial-bank social-engineering OTP/smishing vishing, WhatsApp official/relative impersonation, and motor-vehicle deposit fraud dominate.
cross_border_note: Jamaica (+1-876 and +1-658 overlay) is part of the North American Numbering Plan; lottery scam rings target both US/Canadian seniors and domestic residents while spoofing +1 area codes.

scams.name: Jamaica Lottery / Sweepstakes Advance-Fee Tax & Customs Scam
scams.name_en: Lottery or mobile prize winner scam demanding upfront tax, customs or processing fees
scams.signals_en: Caller claims the recipient won a major sweepstakes, motor vehicle, or BOJ-endorsed mobile prize, demanding upfront processing, tax, or customs fees via wire, remittance, or gift cards before delivery.
scams.legit_en: Legitimate lotteries never require upfront tax or release payments, and Bank of Jamaica confirms it never awards prize cheques for phone competitions.
bait_tactics: Sound thrilled and ask whether they can simply deduct the processing tax straight out of the prize cheque.
Pretend you cannot find a working pen and ask them to spell out the prize department's Kingston street address slowly.
Ask what ticket won because you never recall entering any sweepstakes this year.

scams.name: Jamaican Bank Social-Engineering Vishing & OTP / Token Theft
scams.name_en: Fake local bank security call or smishing follow-up requesting OTP or online banking token
scams.signals_en: Caller poses as a Jamaican commercial bank fraud unit following an SMS alert about a locked account or unauthorized transfer, pressuring the customer to read out an OTP/token or log in via a phishing link.
scams.legit_en: Bank of Jamaica advises that licensed deposit-taking institutions never call or text to ask for passwords, PINs, or one-time security tokens.
bait_tactics: Say your phone screen went dark on speakerphone and ask which parish branch holds your account.
Tell them you are walking past a branch right now and will step inside to verify with a teller.
Pretend the token code has not arrived yet and ask them to explain every step from the beginning.

scams.name: WhatsApp Official / Relative Impersonation & Vehicle Deposit Scam
scams.name_en: WhatsApp impersonation of police officials or relatives and social-media vehicle deposit fraud
scams.signals_en: Fraudster impersonates a senior JCF official, stranded relative on WhatsApp, or cut-price vehicle seller demanding an urgent bank lodge to a mule account or a WhatsApp verification code.
scams.legit_en: JCF officials never solicit funds on WhatsApp, and real vehicle sales or family requests can be verified in person or on saved phone numbers.
bait_tactics: Ask a specific family or neighbourhood question that only your real relative would know.
For a vehicle listing, insist on inspecting the car and fitness papers at a police station lot before paying anything.
Say banking hours just closed for you and ask why the account name does not match the caller's name.
